messages:
yun: ran the adaptive size-aware-decay (SAD) eviction bench across regions + GPUs today. sending quick notes.

mira: nice — main metric? p99 vs hit-rate tradeoff?

yun: baseline = LRU, seg-LRU, and SAD. workload = 3 slen mixes (short-heavy, web-spectrum, long-burst). GPUs: H100 (us-west-2), A10G (eu-central-1).

yun: top-level: SAD gives ~6-9% higher hit rate on web-spectrum at same memory budget, and reduces p99 by ~10-15ms on H100 for slen <= 1024. on A10G improvement smaller (~3-5% hit).

alex: can you paste the p99/throughput numbers? even ballpark is fine.

yun: quick table (SAD vs LRU, web-spectrum, mem budget 4GB):
```
H100: LRU p99=88ms, tps=420 req/s; SAD p99=73ms, tps=450 req/s; hit-rate +8.2%
A10G: LRU p99=120ms, tps=210 req/s; SAD p99=114ms, tps=225 req/s; hit-rate +3.9%
```

yun: for long-burst mix (many slen>2k) SAD hurts a bit on throughput on A10G because eviction churn triggers more kernel launches. H100 handles it better.

benchbot: finished job 1836549123-evict-sad: artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/1836549123/sad-vs-lru.zip (charts + raw csv).

mira: did you try segmented-LRU with prefetcher? we saw gains previously.

yun: yes — seg-LRU+prefetcher nudges hit-rate similar to SAD for short-heavy mix, but on web-spectrum SAD still edges out by ~2%. seg-LRU prefetch increases memory pressure in long-burst and raises p99 tail in A10G.

alex: what about kernel choice? cuBLASLt vs our triton-attn kernels? any interaction?

yun: important: when eviction churn causes more KV shuffles, triton-attn kernels had higher sensitivity to small batch sizes (p99 worsened). on H100 using cuBLASLt-backed matmul reduced the p99 delta by ~7ms. on A10G we didn't see cuBLASLt help as much (driver/rocm differences + kernel path).

mira: any config knobs you recommend for Dedicated pools? autoscale + SAD?

yun: suggestion: enable SAD as default for web-like traffic, keep seg-LRU+prefetch for short-heavy low-latency workloads. For Dedicated A10G fleets, raise batch aggregation timeout by 5-10ms to absorb eviction churn. Also add fallback policy to LRU for sustained long-burst windows.

alex: did you run quantized model variants too? 4-bit jemalloc/quant paths can change KV size.

yun: ran a subset with int4 quant; KV footprint dropped ~28% which further improved hit-rate for same budget — SAD still beneficial but gains compressed (because smaller KVs reduce eviction frequency).

ops-bot: note created: TICKET-1247 -> "Investigate SAD default for web workloads" (assigned to yun). :spiral_note_pad:

mira: can you add the slen distribution files and the run command in the artifact? makes reproducing easier.

yun: yes; command I used:
```
bench run --model=redwood/onnx-ggml-v2 --gpu=h100 --eviction=adaptive-sad --slen-dist=web-spectrum.json --kv-budget=4GB --out=1836549123-out.csv
```

yun: next steps: push quick doc in /docs/kv-eviction/ about config tradeoffs, and schedule a follow-up for Dedicated perf tuning next week.

alex: thanks — can you drop the big chart in #eng-dashboard when available? i'll sync with infra about kernel flags. :thumbsup:
